summary: Bidirectional alignment is nearly complete and solver-visible contracts are well-formed, but recovery of committed DELETE mutations across process restart is a material instruction requirement with no meaningful behavioral test. A solver could omit durable DELETE WAL replay and still pass all 63 probes.

evidence.observation: Sixteen concise bullets plus one short paragraph state writer fencing, precedence, snapshot/scan semantics, conflict rules, commit durability, rollback/kill invisibility, recovery integrity, checkpoint lifecycle, snapshot open rules, STATS/HEALTH, hex/binary limits, protocol resilience, and compatibility preservation.

Delegated contract documents ASCII wire shapes, WAL framing and payload types (PUT/DELETE/COMMIT), snapshot layout, checkpoint publication, HEALTH invariant checks, and stderr behavior for open failures.

35 behavioral probes cover fencing, snapshots, scans, conflicts, torn-tail WAL repair, WAL corruption classes, checkpoint, snapshot integrity, precedence, limits, STATS/HEALTH, hex, and protocol resilience; restart cases exercise PUT commits and torn WAL repair but never a committed DELETE.

19 contract probes add default data-dir ownership, local delete visibility, conflict termination, durable COMMIT ack across kill, multi-commit WAL replay (PUT-only), independent PUT+COMMIT WAL fixture, WAL/snapshot corruption classes, checkpoint interruption recovery, exact READY/HEALTH shapes, C++20/ABI compile checks, and cross-command limit/error consistency.
9 preservation probes cover STONEVAULT_DATA selection, scan-prefix limits, binary round-trip restart (PUT-only), committed hex canonicalization, and additional snapshot corruption classes.

Q4 requires exhaustive forward/reverse matrices, delegated-contract walk, F2P/P2P boundary inspection, ambiguity scan, second omission sweep, and REVISE on any material untested requirement or phantom test contract.

findings.criterion: Every material requirement has meaningful behavioral test coverage (forward matrix completeness)
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires recovery to retain every valid committed transaction and documents DELETE WAL records, but no probe commits a DELETE and restarts (with or without checkpoint) to verify the deletion survives durability/recovery. An implementation that applies DELETE only in-memory or fails to replay DELETE frames would pass all current tests.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add at least one restart probe that seeds a key, commits a DELETE, restarts the engine, and asserts NOT_FOUND/empty scan plus correct sequence; optionally add an independently encoded DELETE+COMMIT WAL fixture mirroring the existing PUT fixture.
findings.regression_risk: Low if added as a new preservation or contract probe without weakening existing corruption or conflict checks.

findings.why_it_matters: Storage-format declares zero-byte declared WAL payload length as intrinsic corruption, but no probe supplies a complete header with payload_length=0; this is a narrow framing edge unlike the DELETE recovery gap.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: add a corruption probe with a complete zero-length framing header expecting fail-closed open.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.gap: Committed DELETE durability across restart is untested; independent WAL fixture covers PUT+COMMIT only.

UNTESTED_REQUIREMENTS: R08: Recovery of a committed DELETE transaction across process restart (WAL replay and/or post-checkpoint snapshot reload) — instruction.md:12 and storage-format.md DELETE payload type are solver-visible but no probe restarts after a successful DELETE commit.

storage-format.md.notes: Wire protocol, WAL/snapshot layouts, HEALTH semantics, and startup precedence are architecture/schema documentation referenced by instruction.md; not a hidden second prompt or repair map.

engine.hpp.notes: C ABI signatures exercised by test_cxx20_sources_and_public_abi_signatures_compile match instruction preservation requirement.
